set.st: April 1964: two men admitted burgling $500 in coins from a Rochelle grocery and said they hid them in a pillowcase under a railroad bridge in town; police never found the coins. The burglars were John Ramsey, 23, and Cecil R. Baker, 22; when police went to the spot, under a rock beneath the CB&Q railroad bridge, they found only the imprints of coins in the mud; the police chief thought children playing there had taken them. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.pl: A CB&Q railroad bridge in Rochelle (the Kyte River crossing is the likely one; not yet confirmed)
pinev: Placed from the source text: GNIS Rochelle; bridge not named
Rockford Register Star, 22 Apr 1964: 'the CB&Q railroad bridge'; the Burlington's Aurora-Savanna line crosses the Kyte River in Rochelle; bridge not yet fixed, pin stays on the town.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: two 1964 items; the coins were already gone when police looked, probably taken by children
